questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Is usually more careful than other drivers.
May take longer to make important decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: May take longer to make important decisions.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers are slower to notice and react to dangers. Drowsy drivers have trouble making important decisions while driving.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. In vehicles that have this, the valve is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: While driving, mirrors should be checked:

options.text: Only if there may be a problem.

questions.explanation: You must know what is around your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors often while driving.

questions.question: When the spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.explanation: Never press the brake pedal when the spring brakes are on. The springs and air pressure together could damage the brakes.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Are not allowed on a vehicle.
Store compressed air for the brakes.
Should be emptied of extra air after each trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Store compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, air storage tanks hold compressed air for the brakes to use. The number and size of tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: Alcohol affects you:
questions.explanation: Alcohol can impair you after just one drink. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while impaired by alcohol.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for the brakes to start working after you press the pedal
The space between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for the brakes to start working after you press the pedal
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the lines to the brakes, so air brakes do not start right away. There is usually at least half a second of brake lag between pressing the pedal and the brakes starting to work.

questions.question: In very hot weather, tires should be checked often because:

options.text: Air pressure may go up as temperature rises.
The tread wears down faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may go up as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases when temperature rises. Pay close attention to tire condition and pressure when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: Air brake systems usually have some water and compressor oil in the compressed air. This water and oil:

options.text: Are needed for the system to work properly.
Should make up about 10 percent of the tank.

questions.explanation: If water and compressor oil build up in an air brake system, they can damage it. Air storage tanks have drains to remove this buildup. Manual drains should be opened at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: If a police officer asks you to take a blood alcohol test:

options.text: You can refuse without any penalty.
You can refuse but must pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL if you refuse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL if you refuse.
questions.explanation: Most states have Implied Consent Laws. By driving on state roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if asked. If you refuse, you will lose your driving privileges. Know the laws in every state where you drive.

questions.question: Why do vehicles use multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions?

options.text: To make the vehicle run more smoothly

questions.explanation: Many vehicles use multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions to provide extra gears.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed to secure a 10-foot cargo load?
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. No matter the cargo size, always use at least two tie-downs.

questions.question: What color light shows that anti-lock brakes are not working?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock brakes have a yellow warning light. It shows when there is a problem with the braking system.

questions.question: How can you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving?

options.text: Engage the clutch halfway before lifting your foot off the brake
Put the vehicle in second gear
Use the parking brake when you stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Engage the clutch halfway before lifting your foot off the brake
questions.explanation: To stop your vehicle from rolling backward when starting after a stop, engage the clutch halfway before removing your foot from the brake pedal.

questions.question: What is a common problem when transporting hanging meat?

options.text: The smell can be a problem

questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity, and the meat swinging can affect how you control the vehicle.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What happens when you overload a vehicle with cargo?

options.text: It affects steering and brake control

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects steering and brake control
questions.explanation: Overloading can harm steering, braking, and speed control. Learn to spot when cargo is overloaded or poorly balanced.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Avoid driving in fog if possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving in fog if possible
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous. Avoid it if you can. If you must drive in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: A 40-foot load should be secured by at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo needs at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: What should you use to put out an electrical fire?
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Do not use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must not roll backwards when you start from a stop. This prevents hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: A driver who is color blind.
A person who does not know the rules of the road.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Stopping at a green light is one sign that a driver may be impaired from alcohol, drugs, sleepiness, or illness.

questions.question: You may be an aggressive driver if you:

options.text: Slow down and maintain a reasonable following distance.
Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by planning for delays, maintaining safe following distances, and not making hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is difficult for the driver to see behind the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front of the vehicle.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
Trailers are not made to be driven in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult for the driver to see behind the trailer.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Only back up when absolutely necessary.

questions.question: Compared to talking on a cell phone while driving, texting while driving is:
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. It distracts your mind and takes your hands and eyes off the road.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, you must pass which endorsement test?
questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries defined hazardous materials.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. This can damage the brakes by combining spring force with air pressure.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is encouraged because:

options.text: The driver will have the best possible view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can offer assistance on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will have the best possible view.
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's left side. This gives you the best view of the rear of your vehicle.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Adjust your driving to match weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your driving to match weather conditions.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, adjust your speed to match conditions. Increase your following distance because it takes longer to stop. Avoid frequent speed changes.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget to check something.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
questions.explanation: Use the same steps every time for your pre-trip inspection. This habit will help you remember to check everything important.

questions.question: If other vehicles are having trouble passing your truck on a road with two or more lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane if your truck is slowing down other traffic. Let other vehicles pass you using the left lane.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Can make a vehicle more likely to tip over.
Is good to use in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make a vehicle more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Place cargo weight as low as possible to prevent tipping.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Check critical items only at the start and end of your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check critical items only at the start and end of your trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during your trip. Watch the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to spot any early warning signs.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should make sure that:

options.text: The pedal surfaces are still grooved and not smoothed out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces are still grooved and not smoothed out.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing is blocking the pedals. Make sure the pedals work properly and have grooved surfaces to prevent slipping.

questions.question: When carrying a sealed load, a driver should:

options.text: Open the load to check safety.
Make sure the weight does not exceed weight limits.
Go through the container before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the weight does not exceed weight limits.
questions.explanation: You cannot open a sealed load to inspect it. However, you must still make sure the load does not exceed weight limits.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: After coming down a steep hill, let your brakes cool before using the parking brake. Using the parking brake on hot brakes can damage them.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: When passing another driver, bicyclist, or pedestrian, always assume they do not see you. This keeps you safe.

questions.question: If you plan to change lanes, your mirrors should:

options.text: Be checked more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked more often than usual.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal driving. Check them even more when you are about to change lanes.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:

options.text: The same as the surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as the surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel at the same speed in the same direction, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives drivers time to see you and move out of your way. Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: When approaching a bridge or overpass, you should:

options.text: Assume the posted clearance height is accurate.
Assume the posted clearance height is inaccurate.
Measure the height of the opening before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the posted clearance height is inaccurate.
questions.explanation: Do not trust posted height clearances. The road may have been repaved or snow may be on the ground, making the actual height different. If you are not sure your vehicle will fit, slow down and find another route.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Always downshift before entering a curve in a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: Heights posted at bridges:
questions.explanation: Posted heights can be wrong. Roads are repaved and snow builds up, changing the actual clearance. Never assume a posted height is correct.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must do everything except:
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass the HazMat test, undergo an FBI fingerprint check, pass a federal background check, and prove U.S. citizenship or permanent residency. A CIA check is not required.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check the tightness of the lug nuts.
See if rocks have gotten into the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the tightness of the lug nuts.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance away to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: In a leaf spring:
questions.explanation: Leaf springs should not have broken or missing leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service until it is fixed.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press down hard for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the pedal returns to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press down hard for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times, then press down hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or another problem.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Are only used on trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Help drivers stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: A driver may have:

options.text: Two licenses: one for cars and one for trucks.
A license for every state where they drive.

questions.explanation: A person can have only one license. Violating this rule can result in jail time and a fine of up to $5,000.
